record.original_question: For population-based metaheuristic algorithms in which multiple search agents form multiple interacting Markov chains, can one develop a mathematical theory that proves convergence and characterizes the rate of convergence for these algorithms, rather than only for the limited few metaheuristics that have already been analyzed mathematically?

evidence.quote: For all population-based metaheuristics, multiple search agents form multiple interacting Markov chains. At the moment, theoretical development in these areas are still at early stage. Therefore, the mathematical analysis concerning of the rate of convergence is very difficult, if not impossible.
Apart from the mathematical analysis on a limited few metaheuristics, convergence of all other algorithms has not been proved mathematically, at least up to now.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A population-based metaheuristic optimization algorithm operates on a finite or measurable search space $S$ by maintaining, at each iteration $t \in \mathbb{N}$, a population $X_t = (x_t^{(1)}, \dots, x_t^{(N)}) \in S^N$ of $N \ge 2$ search agents. The update rule is stochastic: given $X_t$, the next population $X_{t+1}$ is drawn from a transition kernel $P(\,\cdot\, \mid X_t)$ on $S^N$, so that $\{X_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ is a Markov chain on $S^N$ whose coordinates can be viewed as $N$ interacting Markov chains. Let $f : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be an objective function with global minimum value $f^* = \inf_{x\in S} f(x)$, and define the best-so-far value $m_t = \min_{1 \le i \le N} f(x_t^{(i)})$.

Develop a general mathematical theory that, for a broad class of such population-based metaheuristics (including but not limited to genetic algorithms, particle swarm optimization, ant colony optimization, differential evolution, and firefly-type algorithms), accomplishes both of the following:

1. (Convergence) Provides verifiable structural conditions on the kernel $P$ and on $f$ under which $m_t \to f^*$ almost surely (or in probability, or in $L^1$) as $t \to \infty$, or under which the law of $X_t$ converges to a distribution supported on the set of global minimizers.

2. (Rate of convergence) Yields quantitative bounds on the speed of convergence — for instance, explicit upper bounds on $\mathbb{E}[m_t - f^*]$, on the total-variation or Wasserstein distance between the law of $X_t$ and its limiting distribution, or on the expected first hitting time $\tau_\varepsilon = \inf\{t : m_t - f^* \le \varepsilon\}$ — expressed in terms of intrinsic quantities of the algorithm (mixing or contraction coefficients of $P$, spectral data of associated operators, drift functions, population size $N$, dimension and geometry of $S$, and properties of $f$).

The theory should apply uniformly to the multi-agent interacting setting, rather than being restricted to single-chain metaheuristics or to a small list of specific algorithms already analyzed.
artifact.category_tag: Convergence of interacting Markov chains in metaheuristics
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial partial progress exists. Unified Markov-chain frameworks have been developed for randomised search heuristics, including absorbing-Markov-chain models, spectral-radius criteria (convergence iff ρ(Q)<1), average drift analysis, backward drift analysis, and average convergence rate bounds, as well as Markov-chain analyses of specific genetic algorithms and local search methods. However, a single uniform quantitative convergence-rate theory covering all population-based metaheuristics with interacting agents has not been established; the program remains active and only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: A Unified Markov Chain Approach to Analysing Randomised Search Heuristics
status_evidence.snippet: A unified Markov chain approach for studying the convergence, convergence rate and expected hitting time of randomised search heuristics; convergence iff spectral radius ρ(Q)<1; average/backward drift analysis introduced.
status_evidence.claim: General Markov-chain convergence and rate frameworks have been developed for randomised search heuristics, demonstrating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Convergence Analysis of Metaheuristics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey chapter on convergence analyses of various metaheuristic algorithms.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence analyses exist for several metaheuristic families, but a fully general theory remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Modeling Local Search Metaheuristics Using Markov Decision Processes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work modelling local search metaheuristics via Markov decision processes.
status_evidence.claim: Research into rigorous Markov-based models of metaheuristics is ongoing in 2024, indicating the broader theory is still being developed.
